questions.q: What are the three ego states Berne says everyone moves between?
a: Parent, Adult and Child
Id, ego and superego
Past, present and future
Rational, emotional and social
questions.why: The first lesson says each person's behavior falls into one of these three recurring patterns.

questions.q: What does the Child ego state represent?
a: The spontaneous emotions and intimacy we are born with
The rules we learned from our parents
The logic we use to solve problems
The mask we show to strangers
questions.why: The first lesson says the Child is buried under the other states and surfaces in moments like sex.

questions.q: When are you playing a game, according to the summary?
a: When you seem to be in one ego state but are really in another
When you compete with a coworker for a promotion
When you lie to get something you want
When you avoid talking about your feelings
questions.why: The second lesson defines a game as a hidden mismatch between the state you show and the state you act from.

questions.q: In the game called Alcoholic, what does the drinker actually get from her family?
a: Fuel for self-pity that leads to more drinking
A genuine cure for her addiction
Attention from a sympathetic doctor
Protection from her own worst impulses
questions.why: The second lesson says the family's scolding is exactly the payoff the rebellious Child is looking for.

questions.q: Why do people keep playing games even when the games hurt them?
a: Games let them avoid being vulnerable
Games always get them what they want
They never notice the cost of a game
Games make them more likable to others
questions.why: The third lesson says dropping games means revealing your true self, which is why it feels so difficult.
